issues.legal_issue: A disputed will was genuinely executed by the testator and attested in his presence.
material_facts: The testator signed every page of the will and a note listing corrections.
He personally presented the will for registration, admitted its execution before the registrar, and signed again in the registrar’s presence.
Two attesting witnesses testified that the testator signed in their presence and that they then attested in his presence.
The court accepted the signatures attributed to the testator’s wife and daughter-in-law as genuine, having considered the family letters and evidence about their relationship with the beneficiary.
A handwriting expert gave a contrary opinion, but the court considered handwriting comparison uncertain and not conclusive.
issues.conclusion: The evidence established that the testator executed the will and that the disputed signatures of the two family members were genuine; the accepted witness evidence supported due attestation.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed execution and attestation from the document, registration endorsements, witness testimony, and surrounding evidence. It treated handwriting comparison as an imperfect science and the expert opinion as non-conclusive. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this determination.

rule.if: probate_appeal and testator_signed_will and testator_acknowledged_execution_during_registration and credible_attestors_confirmed_execution_and_attestation and surrounding_evidence_supported_disputed_signatures

predicates.probate_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether a will should be admitted to probate.
predicates.testator_signed_will: The testator signed the will, including its pages or other parts showing that he adopted the document.
predicates.testator_acknowledged_execution_during_r: The testator personally presented the will for registration and acknowledged its execution before the registrar.
predicates.credible_attestors_confirmed_execution_a: Credible attesting witnesses testified that the testator signed in their presence and that they attested in his presence.
predicates.surrounding_evidence_supported_disputed_: Evidence about the document and the parties’ circumstances supported the authenticity of signatures challenged as forged.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning probate involves a will personally signed and acknowledged by the testator, credible testimony supports execution and attestation, and surrounding evidence supports challenged signatures, execution and attestation are established.

issues.legal_issue: Suspicious circumstances surrounding a will do not prevent probate when the evidence as a whole dispels the suspicion.
material_facts: The testator lived for nearly four years after executing and registering the will and did not revoke or cancel it.
The testator personally arranged for registration at his residence, and the registration endorsements confirmed his presentation and acknowledgment of the will.
The will left the estate to a child who had been raised and genuinely loved as a member of the family.

The wife and daughter-in-law were not separately provided for, but the evidence showed that the family treated the beneficiary as their own child and that the daughter-in-law and the beneficiary’s mother managed the family estate without conflict.

The trial court granted probate, but the High Court set that grant aside on the basis of suspicious circumstances, including disputed signatures and the absence of separate provision for the wife and daughter-in-law.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances identified as suspicious were dispelled by the evidence; the appeal was allowed, the High Court judgment was set aside, and the trial court’s grant of probate was restored.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered suspicious circumstances in light of the whole evidentiary record, including the testator’s personal execution and registration of the will, his failure to revoke it during his lifetime, and the family circumstances explaining the disposition. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this determination.

rule.if: probate_appeal and testator_personally_registered_will and no_revocation_during_extended_survival and family_evidence_explained_omitted_provisions and evidence_as_a_whole_dispelled_suspicion

predicates.probate_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether a will should be admitted to probate.
predicates.testator_personally_registered_will: The testator personally arranged for registration of the will and acknowledged its execution during that process.
predicates.no_revocation_during_extended_survival: The testator lived for a substantial period after making the will and took no step to revoke or cancel it.
predicates.family_evidence_explained_omitted_provis: Evidence of the family relationships and arrangements gave context for the will’s failure to make separate provision for certain family members.
predicates.evidence_as_a_whole_dispelled_suspicion: The evidence considered together answered the concerns raised about the will’s genuineness or circumstances.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning probate concerns a personally registered will that remained unrevoked during the testator’s extended survival, and family evidence and the record as a whole dispel the suspicions raised, the probate grant is upheld.
